requirements.requirement: Healthy 3-member etcd cluster running across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: member list (cmd-fc4ea76d687344a5) shows all 3 members started and endpoint health true for all 3 endpoints; 4 application keys written on node1 (cmd-60ed27063d8747f3) and confirmed readable via replication on node3 (cmd-28563df08d5c4e1f).

requirements.requirement: node3 member permanently lost (data unrecoverable) while cluster quorum/availability preserved
requirements.summary: etcd stopped, disabled, and data directory wiped on node3 (cmd-5ca5818a56e545db); immediately after, node1/node2 endpoints report healthy, node3 endpoint unreachable (connection refused), and application keys remain readable via node1 (cmd-beb9d5c3117a4edf), directly demonstrating the bounded disruption with quorum preserved.

requirements.requirement: Dead member removed from cluster membership and replaced with a new working member on the same node3 system
requirements.summary: Old member 551e3d60e1e0c3b9 removed via etcdctl (cmd-9bce2d6e378f42e3); new member added for node3 with new ID 87e9d437b9aadf7d (cmd-96b4aa8d858e4069); node3 restarted with initial-cluster-state=existing and etcd reports active (cmd-e661ffae9f304fcd).

requirements.requirement: Cluster restored to three healthy members with existing keys intact after replacement
requirements.summary: endpoint health true for all 3 endpoints and member list shows 3 started members including the new node3 ID (cmd-aed66198f3c44a78); node3 directly returns all 4 original application keys via its new member (cmd-8afdd8f34b2544ff), confirming raft sync and data integrity.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show the full transition: baseline boot ids (cmd-9bbe0f6c46644a7f, cmd-79d6a0e1ab2148d5, cmd-8f0587e1c2fa45b7) match the fixed before_prepare boot-identity snapshots; reboot acknowledgements issued sequentially one node at a time preserving quorum (cmd-7934b19b7e914d1a, cmd-ab8de7e48e654f6b, cmd-e32537a636b8438f); changed boot ids observed post-restart (cmd-35c4969f2148407c, cmd-3d2e6fb4ee9b4c7c, cmd-d78bc44bac844c8d) matching the fixed after_executor snapshots exactly; and recovered etcd active state, 3/3 member health, and intact application keys confirmed after each restart (cmd-815bb4ba86214cb1, cmd-f8ca530729104b8e, cmd-cc16f36325504186).

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task contract: it established a healthy 3-member etcd cluster with application keys, directly demonstrated node3's permanent loss with quorum preserved on node1/node2, removed the dead member and added a working replacement member on node3, and directly confirmed the cluster returned to 3/3 healthy members with all original keys intact and replicated to the new node3 member. The independent, mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed to a high standard on all three nodes, with pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity (cross-checked exactly against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and recovered cluster/data state each directly observed. Hygiene is good overall; the only blemish is unreverted temporary install artifacts left in /tmp on each node and one benign systemd readiness timeout during initial bootstrap that self-resolved.
limitations: No evidence was captured of etcd's internal raft/member-sync logs during the node3 rejoin beyond endpoint status and key reads, so the exact resynchronization mechanism (snapshot vs. log replay) is inferred rather than directly observed, though the outcome (data present, correct raft indices) is directly confirmed.

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical aliases (prepare disabled), so no preparer-introduced state could be distinguished from executor changes; all after_executor deltas are attributable to the executor by elimination.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. Installation, systemd unit creation, firewalld port openings, user/directory creation, cluster bootstrap, the intentional node3 data-loss simulation, member remove/add, and the sequential node reboots all have a clear causal role in either satisfying the task or the mandatory restart protocol; no unnecessary or unexplained mutations, troubleshooting experiments, failed services, or weakened security controls were found. One state-changing action, the initial 'systemctl enable --now etcd' on node1 (cmd-f33a91e298ed4418), returned exit code 3 with 'Job for etcd.service failed because a timeout was exceeded' — expected behavior for a Type=notify etcd unit waiting on quorum from not-yet-started peers, not a failure requiring remediation, and etcd was confirmed active and healthy 5 seconds later (cmd-e8e6d4067c804cda). Minor unreverted residue: downloaded etcd.tar.gz and extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64/ build artifacts were left in /tmp on all three nodes (visible in after_executor temporary-files snapshots), a low-risk, low-severity leftover from installation rather than a broad or destructive change. No failed services, no package-manager inconsistency, and no unsafe network exposure were introduced (firewalld ports opened are required for etcd cluster operation).
